Hi Priya / Alex,

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (top-level):
- Goal: Replace current FAQ search with a RAG assistant that reliably grounds answers to Acme docs and reduces time-to-resolution for support agents.
- Primary success metrics you mentioned: Recall@10 for retrieval (target >= 0.85 on internal eval set), grounding precision (percentage of answers that cite high-confidence sources) >= 0.9, and median token inference latency <= 120ms for the generation step.

Initial recommendations (model + infra):
- Retriever: bi-encoder (dense) built on sentence-transformers, candidate model: "sentence-transformers/multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-v2" for fast recall.
- Reranker: start with our lightweight reranker ("redwood/reranker-lite-v1") for production baseline, fall back to a cross-encoder for high-importance queries during POC ("cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2").
- Generator: for best tradeoff, try "redwood/retrieval-llama-13b-q4" (quantized) — good latency on Dedicated A100 / T4; also evaluate an open-chat variant for safety/regulatory comparisons.

Suggested retrieval settings to evaluate in POC:
- chunk_size: 500 tokens, chunk_overlap: 50 tokens
- retriever_top_k_candidates: 50 (pool for reranker)
- reranker_top_k: 5 (final passages sent to generator)
- caching: prefix KV caching + query result caching for hot queries

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached:
- ACME_RAG_POC_plan.pdf (high-level plan + timeline)
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (initial prompt + eval prompts)
- redwood_rag_benchmarks_q3_2027.csv (sample benchmark runs against similar corpora)

Links:
- Internal benchmark dashboard: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/rag-acme-2027
- Shared drive with prompt sets & eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-acme-2027

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (30m) to validate retriever / reranker tradeoffs and confirm metrics to measure.
2) Run a focused eval over your 1k golden queries (we can run MRR, Recall@K, grounding precision).
3) Pilot on Dedicated with A/B vs your current FAQ pipeline.

Available times from my side: Tue/Wed 10-12 PT or Thu 1-3 PT. If you prefer, we can loop in Rishi (ML Eng) and Monica (CS) for the technical session.

Thanks,

Priya — thanks for the questions. Short answers and a couple more resources below.

1) Latency / cost (rough production guidance):
- reranker-lite: ~8-20ms per query on T4/A10x (batched), cost is low — good for 95% of queries.
- cross-encoder (ms-marco style): ~60-150ms per query on A100 (quantized 8-bit) depending on batch and sequence length — much higher compute cost but significantly higher rank quality.

Our recommended approach for the POC: use reranker-lite by default, and route a configurable % (or only high-importance queries flagged by intent) to the cross-encoder. That gives predictable latency and a path to improve grounding on the high-value traffic.

2) Grounding precision definition we use: percentage of generated answers that include at least one cited passage where a simple exact/fuzzy match verifies the generated claim against the source text. We flag "possible hallucinations" when the generator output contains claims not present in any top-10 retrieved chunks. We also compute an evidence-confidence score from the reranker.

3) Golden queries: you can upload the 1k set to the shared Drive link (prompt_set_v1.jsonl) or share a secure S3 link — we'll run the eval in our harness and share MRR/Recall@K, grounding precision, and per-query logs.

Pre-reads / resources:
- Small benchmark summary (attached redwood_rag_benchmarks_q3_2027.csv).
- Eval harness readme: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmark-acme-2027/readme.txt

Rishi / Monica — tagging you for any notes on the reranker thresholds, compute estimates, and suggested A/B experiment setup.

I'll hold Wed 10:30 PT — sending calendar invite after we confirm.

Cheers,
Marissa

Quick internal notes / plan for the Wed deep-dive: 

- Reranker strategy: start with reranker-lite (cheap) + sampling of top traffic to cross-encoder. Concrete thresholds: if reranker-lite score < 0.45 OR query flagged as "high importance" by Priya's team, send to cross-encoder. We'll tune threshold after initial runs.

- Metrics we'll present: MRR, Recall@1/5/10, grounding_precision (exact/fuzzy citation match ratio), and a "Hallucination rate" computed by mismatch between generated claims and cited passages. We'll also include per-query latency P50/P95 for both components.

- Retrieval settings to test in POC: chunk_size=500 / overlap=50, retriever_top_k=50, reranker_top_k=5. We'll include an ablation with top_k 100 and chunk_size 250 to see sensitivity.

- Compute / cost notes: quantized cross-encoder on A100 gives best latency (~60ms p50) but higher cost; we can CPU-host reranker-lite for minimal cost. For the pilot, estimate ~1.8x incremental compute cost over current FAQ pipeline (detailed calc in the POC plan).

I'll prepare: sample eval runs (MRR/Recall tables), per-query logs for a 200-query pilot, and a short cost estimate slide. Monica — can you confirm CS acceptance criteria for the pilot (e.g., grounding_precision >= 0.9 & user satisfaction lift)?
